texts: summary.md reports counts per IMP item, with no column for verification status.
summary.md tables count reasons per improvement item, with no column for verification status.
five-whys is a personal RedJay plugin with no other contributors or reviewers.
Five-whys is a personal plugin in the RedJay marketplace, which has no contributor pool to draw reviewers from.
Version bumps are hand edits to plugin.json and the marketplace entry, so no tool invokes the checklist.
Version bumps are hand edits to plugin.json and the RedJay marketplace entry, with no release script.
test_docs.py confirms flags named in SKILL.md exist, not that a reader maps them correctly.
test_docs.py checks that flags named in SKILL.md exist in the script, not that omissions are intentional.
The v0.2.0 branch was merged locally into main with no pull request, so no review thread could flag the gap.
The feature branch was merged locally into main with no pull request that could gather review.
Claude Code's /plugin install copies the repository into a cache with no step that installs Python packages.
Plugin installation copies the repository into the cache and runs no build or pip step.
tests.yml runs only unittest on Python 3.9 and 3.12, with no benchmarking or size-tracking job.
The tests.yml CI matrix runs bare unittest on Python 3.9 and 3.12 with no requirements file.
The ledger entry schema holds only id, d and note, with no field for a covering code.
The ledger row holds only id, code, note and text, with no weight or secondary code field.
Branch protection on GitHub is not configured, so main accepts pushes without required reviews or checks.
main accepts direct local merges with no branch protection, so no reviewer is structurally required.
Merge commit b54d36d landed seconds after its feature commit c768cb2, leaving no review step between them.
b54d36d merged 11 seconds after c768cb2 committed, leaving no interval for inspection between them.
3,905 reasons yield about 7.6 million pairs, too many for pure-Python cosine loops at assembly.
Labeling paraphrases means comparing reasons pairwise, and 3,905 reasons yield about 7.6 million pairs to consider.
The Agent tool is available to models, not to Python, so fivewhys.py cannot dispatch subagents.
fivewhys.py can emit task lists but cannot launch Claude subagents, so dispatch is inherently a model tool call.
RedJay is the author's own marketplace, so no maintainer outside the project reviews submissions.
The RedJay marketplace is the author's own listing, so it brings no outside reviewers.
The repository root holds README, RELEASING and LICENSE only, with no CHANGELOG file.
No CHANGELOG exists, so readers have no release timestamps to compare with the table's date.
The show subcommand prints requested subtrees but offers no random sample for spot review.
index.md presents the tree by level but offers no sampling view for spot-checking quickly.
Every branch prompt repeats the full user context and evidence list instead of referencing one shared copy.
fivewhys.py copies one identical problem and context block into all 26 generated prompts.
RELEASING.md item 4 requires reading the tree, so reaching readable output quickly took priority.
RELEASING.md item 4 requires reading the tree but not recording what the reading found.
RELEASING.md gates version bumps on tests, validation and smoke runs, with no item reviewing a release's motivating evidence.
RELEASING.md gates releases on tests, validation, smoke runs and version matching, never on surface area.
Cost estimates and sibling-aware prompts were separate catalog items, implemented and reviewed independently.
Wave capping and sibling-aware prompts were separate catalog items implemented without examining their interaction.
The split default came from v0.1.0 and was not revisited when sibling-aware prompts arrived in v0.2.0.
v0.1.0 split script-for-data from skill-for-flow, and v0.2.0 extended that split without revisiting it.
The regex tokenizer does no stemming, so estimate, estimates and estimated count as different tokens.
Lexical matching has no synonym table, so pairs like cost and tokens or eval and test never link.
Item 6 compares plugin.json with the marketplace entry only, never with the version behind the measurements.
Item 6 requires only matching versions in plugin.json and the RedJay marketplace entry to publish.
GitHub deliberately hides repository secrets from pull_request workflows triggered by forks.
pull_request_target would expose secrets to untrusted code, unsafe for an agent holding Bash.
index.md lays out levels but no sampled view, so reading beyond it means opening the raw tree.
